text:
Alex: Heads-up: after yesterday's merge to routing we are seeing a 15-25% P95 latency regression in the A arm of the rollout. Not catastrophic but consistent across p95/p99.
deploy-bot: DEPLOY: commit 32a9f6f merged to canary-A (route: kernel-routing-v2). CI perf checks passed earlier.
Maria: Which metric dashboard? p95 tokens or end-to-end?
Alex: End-to-end inference latency (API -> first byte). Token-level looks fine but KV cache hit rate dropped ~6% on canary-A.
Kevin: Did the merge touch KV eviction or kernel hint selection? I recall a fallback change.
Samir: It updated kernel routing to prefer the new tiled-attn kernel for short sequences; added a fallback path if tiled kernel fails. Also adjusted steady-state batching heuristics to be slightly more aggressive.
Lina: I pulled flame graphs for a sample request: big uptick in kernel selection overhead and a spike in fallback invocations. Paste:```flame: kernel_route_select +45ms; tiled_kernel_init +12ms; fallback_switch +30ms; kv_lookup +2ms```
Maria: So the tiled kernel init + fallback path is adding ~30ms tail for some requests. That explains p95. Can we quantify how many requests hit fallback?
Samir: Telemetry shows fallback_rate increased from 0.3% -> 3.7% on canary-A. Mostly on seq_len < 32 where tiled kernel path races with KV prefetch.
Alex: We should gate the rollout and start a bisect. Can we pause A/B traffic to A? If A is paused, we revert to B which is stable.
sre-bot: ACTION: pausing split traffic to canary-A. Traffic rebalanced to canary-B at 14:12 UTC.
Kevin: For immediate mitigation we can disable tiled kernel auto-select in the routing layer (config flag) which should avoid init+fallback cost. Low risk toggle.
Lina: I'll prepare a quick config flip and run a 10m smoke. If that stabilizes p95, we can unpause.
Samir: Also we should bisect the merge to find the exact commit adding the fallback switch. I can do a git bisect across the last 8 commits.
Maria: Also need to add a CI perf test to catch fallback hot paths. Current CI only checks token throughput not selection overhead.
Alex: Good call. Lina, coordinate with Samir to test config flip. Kevin, open a perf-bug and add CI perf test item. Samir, run bisect and share culprit commit. Use /incident to track.
Lina: Flip deployed to canary-A config in staging flag `runtime.tiled_kernel_auto=false`. Running smoke now.
Lina: Smoke: p95 back to baseline within 3 minutes. KV hit-rate restored. No functional errors.
Alex: Nice. Unpause rollout? Or keep paused until bisect complete?
Kevin: Keep paused. We need root cause and a follow-up that either defers tiled kernel init or makes fallback cheap.
Samir: Bisect result: commit 7d5c4b2 introduced the fallback switch and non-blocking init. The race condition was that the tiled init path sometimes returns an 'incomplete' token and triggers fallback code path synchronously. I'll open PR to make tiled init truly async + add guard to avoid sync fallback.
Maria: Add perf test: synthetic short-seq workloads that assert fallback_rate < 0.5%. Put it in canary CI gates.
Alex: Thanks. Owners: Samir (fix PR + bisect notes), Kevin (perf test + ticket), Lina (rollback config + validation). I'll keep thread open until PR merged. :thumbsup:
Samir: Created PR #4821 with fix + tests. Request review.
Kevin: Perf test added to ci/perf/canary_short_seq. Running in nightly.
deploy-bot: DEPLOY: config flip applied to canary-A (runtime.tiled_kernel_auto=false).
Lina: Re-enabled traffic to canary-A at 15:03 UTC after confirming p95 stable for 30m with config flip.
Alex: Once Samir's PR merged and CI perf passes, we should revert config flip and re-run A/B with stricter SLO gate (p95 delta < 5% and fallback_rate < 0.5%).
Maria: Also add alert for sudden fallback_rate > 1% during rollouts.
sre-bot: NOTE: alert rule created: runtime.fallback_rate > 1% for 5m.
Alex: Great. Closing actionables: track PR, CI perf, revert config, tighten gate. Thanks team.
